taskVersion.name: deadline-math-reasoned
taskVersion.description: Standard set, reasoning allowed. Convert a published contest deadline to the reader's local time: day rollover, the weeks when the EU and US change clocks on different dates, 12 AM and AoE wording, non-hour offsets. Ground truth from zoneinfo.

parts.text:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close September 30, 2026 at 5:00 PM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On September 30, 2026, Eastern Time is in Daylight Saving Time (EDT, UTC-4), and Madrid is observing Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2). 

5:00 PM EDT is 21:00 UTC, which corresponds to 23:00 CEST on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-09-30 23:00

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: July 15, 2026, 12:00 UTC."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Lima, Peru is in the Peru Time (PET) zone, which is UTC-5 year-round (no daylight saving time). 

Subtracting 5 hours from 12:00 UTC on July 15, 2026 gives 07:00 on July 15, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-07-15 07:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Applications are due June 1, 2026 at 9:00 AM CEST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

CEST (Central European Summer Time) is UTC+2, while Tokyo operates on JST (Japan Standard Time), which is UTC+9. Tokyo is 7 hours ahead of CEST. 

Adding 7 hours to 9:00 AM on June 1, 2026 gives 4:00 PM (16:00) on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-06-01 16:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The contest ends on October 11, 2026 at 11:59 PM PDT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To convert the contest deadline to your local time in Madrid:

1. **PDT (Pacific Daylight Time)** is UTC−7.
2. On October 11, 2026, Madrid will be observing **CEST (Central European Summer Time)**, which is UTC+2 (Daylight Saving Time in Spain ends on October 25, 2026).
3. The time difference between PDT and CEST is **+9 hours**.
4. Adding 9 hours to October 11, 2026, at 11:59 PM (23:59) PDT results in October 12, 2026, at 08:59 CEST.

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 08:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 3, 2026 at 11:59 PM PST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

March 3, 2026 at 11:59 PM PST is UTC-8. Madrid is on Central European Time (CET, UTC+1) on that date, which is 9 hours ahead of PST. Adding 9 hours to March 3, 2026, 23:59 gives March 4, 2026, 08:59.

ANSWER: 2026-03-04 08:59

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "Deadline: 10:00 AM CET, February 2, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To convert the deadline to your local time in Los Angeles:

1. Central European Time (CET) is UTC+1.
2. Los Angeles is in the Pacific Time Zone, observing Pacific Standard Time (PST, UTC-8) in February.
3. PST is 9 hours behind CET (UTC+1 to UTC-8).
4. Subtracting 9 hours from 10:00 AM CET on February 2, 2026, results in 1:00 AM PST on February 2, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-02-02 01:00

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Submit by 8:00 AM JST on May 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Japan Standard Time (JST) is UTC+9, while Lima, Peru is on Peru Time (PET), which is UTC-5 year-round. This makes Lima 14 hours behind JST. 

Subtracting 14 hours from 8:00 AM on May 5, 2026 gives 6:00 PM on May 4, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-05-04 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 28, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To determine the deadline in Madrid, Spain:

1. **Pacific Time (PT) on October 28, 2026:**
   The United States observes Pacific Daylight Time (PDT, UTC-7) until November 1, 2026. Therefore, 11:59 PM PT is 23:59 PDT (UTC-7), which corresponds to 06:59 UTC on October 29, 2026.

2. **Madrid Local Time on October 29, 2026:**
   Daylight saving time in Europe ends on the last Sunday of October (October 25, 2026). As a result, Madrid will be on Central European Time (CET, UTC+1). 

3. **Conversion:**
   06:59 UTC + 1 hour = 07:59 CET on October 29, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 07:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The live session starts October 30, 2026, 9:00 AM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On October 30, 2026:
- The US is observing Eastern Daylight Time (EDT, UTC-4), so 9:00 AM EDT is 13:00 UTC.
- Spain (and the EU) transitioned out of daylight saving time on the last Sunday of October (October 25, 2026), meaning Madrid is observing Central European Time (CET, UTC+1).

Adding 1 hour to 13:00 UTC gives 14:00 local time in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-10-30 14:00

I live in New York, USA. A contest page says: "Voting closes October 27, 2026 at 18:00 CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On October 27, 2026, Central Europe is on Central European Time (CET, UTC+1) as European daylight saving time ends on October 25, 2026. New York is still observing Eastern Daylight Time (EDT, UTC-4) until November 1, 2026. 

The time difference between CET (UTC+1) and EDT (UTC-4) is 5 hours. Subtracting 5 hours from 18:00 CET yields 13:00 EDT.

ANSWER: 2026-10-27 13:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Final round closes November 2, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To convert the deadline to your local time in Madrid:

1. **Pacific Time (PT)**: In the United States, Daylight Saving Time ends on Sunday, November 1, 2026. Therefore, on November 2, 2026, PT is in Pacific Standard Time (PST), which is UTC-8.
   - 11:59 PM PST on November 2, 2026 = 07:59 UTC on November 3, 2026.

2. **Madrid Time**: In Spain, Daylight Saving Time ends on Sunday, October 25, 2026. Therefore, on November 3, 2026, Madrid is on Central European Time (CET), which is UTC+1.
   - 07:59 UTC + 1 hour = 08:59 CET on November 3, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-11-03 08:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 20, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On March 20, 2026, the United States is observing Pacific Daylight Time (PDT, UTC-7), as daylight saving time begins on March 8, 2026. 

Spain does not begin daylight saving time until March 29, 2026, meaning Madrid is observing Central European Time (CET, UTC+1). 

Madrid is 8 hours ahead of Pacific Time:
- March 20, 2026, at 11:59 PM PDT + 8 hours = March 21, 2026, at 07:59 CET.

ANSWER: 2026-03-21 07:59

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "The webinar starts March 25, 2026, 12:00 PM CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On March 25, 2026, Central European Time (CET) is UTC+1, while Los Angeles is on Pacific Daylight Time (PDT), which is UTC-7 (Daylight Saving Time begins on March 8, 2026, in the US). 

The time difference between CET and PDT is 8 hours:
12:00 PM CET minus 8 hours is 4:00 AM PDT.

ANSWER: 2026-03-25 04:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 AM ET on October 12, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To determine the deadline in Madrid time:

1. **Eastern Time (ET)**: On October 12, 2026, the United States is in Daylight Saving Time (EDT), which is UTC-4. 
   - 12:00 AM ET is midnight at the start of October 12, 2026 (00:00 EDT), corresponding to 04:00 UTC on October 12, 2026.

2. **Madrid, Spain**: On October 12, 2026, Spain observes Central European Summer Time (CEST), which is UTC+2.
   - Adding 2 hours to 04:00 UTC gives 06:00 on October 12, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 06:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Papers are due October 9, 2026 (23:59 AoE)."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

AoE (Anywhere on Earth) corresponds to the UTC-12 time zone. 
- October 9, 2026, at 23:59 AoE is equivalent to October 10, 2026, at 11:59 UTC.
- On October 10, 2026, Madrid is observing Central European Summer Time (CEST), which is UTC+2.
- Adding 2 hours to 11:59 UTC gives 13:59 on October 10, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-10 13:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Registration closes 12:00 PM PT, August 14, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On August 14, 2026, Pacific Time (PT) observes Pacific Daylight Time (PDT, UTC-7), and Madrid, Spain observes Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2). 

12:00 PM PDT corresponds to 19:00 UTC. Adding 2 hours for Madrid's local daylight saving time gives 21:00 on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-08-14 21:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 11:59 PM IST, November 10, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To convert the deadline to your local time in Madrid, Spain:

1. **Given deadline:** November 10, 2026, at 11:59 PM (23:59) Indian Standard Time (IST, UTC+5:30).
2. **Convert to UTC:** 23:59 − 5 hours 30 minutes = 18:29 UTC on November 10, 2026.
3. **Convert to Madrid local time:** On November 10, Spain observes Central European Time (CET, UTC+1). 
   - 18:29 UTC + 1 hour = 19:29 CET on November 10, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-11-10 19:29

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Submissions close at 5:00 PM Nepal time on April 2, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To find the deadline in Lima, Peru (UTC-5), we can convert Nepal Time (NPT, UTC+5:45) to your local time:

1. **Nepal Deadline:** April 2, 2026, at 17:00 (UTC+5:45)
2. **Convert to UTC:** 17:00 minus 5 hours and 45 minutes = 11:15 UTC on April 2, 2026
3. **Convert UTC to Lima Time (UTC-5):** 11:15 minus 5 hours = 06:15 on April 2, 2026

ANSWER: 2026-04-02 06:15

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Applications close 10:00 AM Adelaide time, October 6, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To convert 10:00 AM Adelaide time on October 6, 2026, to Madrid time:

1. **Adelaide Time Zone:** Daylight saving time in South Australia begins on the first Sunday of October (October 4, 2026), making Adelaide UTC+10:30 (ACDT).
2. **Madrid Time Zone:** Madrid observes Central European Summer Time (CEST) until the last Sunday of October, making it UTC+2:00.
3. **Time Difference:** Adelaide is 8 hours and 30 minutes ahead of Madrid.
4. **Conversion:** Subtracting 8 hours and 30 minutes from 10:00 AM on October 6, 2026, gives 1:30 AM on October 6, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-06 01:30

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close 6:00 PM Sydney time on October 3, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To find the deadline in Madrid's local time:

1. **Sydney Time Zone (AEST):** Daylight saving time in New South Wales begins on the first Sunday of October, which falls on October 4 in 2026. Therefore, on Saturday, October 3, 2026, Sydney is still on Australian Eastern Standard Time (AEST), which is UTC+10. 
   - 6:00 PM (18:00) AEST is 08:00 UTC.

2. **Madrid Time Zone (CEST):** Spain observes Central European Summer Time (CEST), which is UTC+2, until the last Sunday of October.
   - 08:00 UTC corresponds to 10:00 CEST.

ANSWER: 2026-10-03 10:00
